record_notes.DCP-LETT-1806: Supplied February 1856 conjectured from travel and Lyell meeting; both surviving blocks, all five notes, annotations and bibliography read. Beginning and ending missing. Intended live rabbits died; adult Porto Santo rabbits now in spirits with other shot pair, eel found by Wollaston but offered through Lowe, and introduced Madeira frogs in separate bottle. Collection/preparation is completed, forwarding awaits Darwin directions, not proven delivery. Frog introduction within fifty years and origin Canary/England uncertain. Later Variation narrative and April conversation are separate witnesses, not reconstructed missing letter text. Source runs aboutthe/inislands retained as transcription artifacts.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1893: June 6, supplied 1856; all three blocks, twelve notes, long quoted Darwin note on Lyell, and bibliography read. Thanks missing Wollaston cover and Lyell letter, but only less than half through Wollaston book; reading-notebook entry June 5 does not prove completion. Legitimate variation teasing, minority argument and Unitarian feather-bed analogy occur in discussion of species limits. Editorial summary asserts religious change, while body does not establish a factual conversion away from Christianity; preserve actual analogy and do not turn summary into Darwin voice. Future hostile Origin review described in apparatus, with bibliography instead listing an 1860 Curculionidae article; mismatch held, not harmonised. Forwarding to Lyell is reported attached-cover provenance, not an incoming source available here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1912: June 27, supplied 1856 from Darwin annotation; both surviving incomplete blocks, four notes, annotations and bibliography read. Begins mid-sentence with digestive joke. Explicit question about other insect orders is missing; no such question in June 6 letter. Other orders apparently less anomalous than Coleoptera; hypothetical former Atlantic beetle/snail province defended humorously, not established continent. Top annotation June27/56 establishes a knowledge bound, not independently a precise Wollaston writing or arrival day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1912A: Circa June 27, 1856, despite exact-looking XML endpoints; three incomplete blocks, all three notes including quoted Darwin book annotation, separate manuscript marks and bibliography read. Different paper proves not the same physical letter as 1912 per apparatus. Size differences and intermediate links, possible inbreeding-related deterioration despite numerous progeny, and partial bulk compensation for wing loss all qualified hypotheses. Missing opening and ending, no precise arrival or merge into companion letter. Darwin muscles-abort note undated and separate voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2030: Early November 1856 conjectured from snail experiments; all seven surviving blocks, eight notes, annotations and bibliography read. XML spans entire November, not exact early-month day. Scarites mandibles and reduced Meloe wing-cases variable; elytral connateness is a character rather than organ, Harpalus vividus not invariant; suggested tropical studies prospective. Tarphius spine not observed variable and probably sexual, a stated counterqualification. Snails wished alive except in salt water; no result in this letter. Beginning missing and Darwin detailed query absent. Undated Q/portfolio and whole-genus note separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2013: December 11 or 18, 1856 discrete Thursday alternatives, not continuous dates; all six blocks, seven notes including full experimental-book excerpt, annotations and bibliography read. Congratulates sixth son and jokes about supposedly badly behaved surviving snails; sex symbols male/female meaningful, not species labels. Collection in second week May1855 does not date Darwin receipt. Miocene patriarchs and ten years in diabolical seawater are playful extrapolation, not an observed ten-year survival. Other specimens largely dead. Lowe endemic Vitrina versus Wollaston insular-modification view and possible human/sea transport all qualified. Raw apparatus has three true MathML halves: smaller half, 9½ A.M., other larger half; flattened 12/912 must not become quantities twelve/912. Actual trial notes and later Origin belong separate source layers.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2076: Easter Sunday April12, supplied1857; all nine long blocks, fourteen notes, annotations and bibliography read. Missing Darwin note arrived to Wollaston April11 late night, not Darwin receipt of this answer. Health advice and hoped Catalogue completion separate from October publication. P3 full family/genus inventory read: genuine no detections, single specimens, possible imports, low frequency and representative apterous genera are distinct. Absence of strong flyers has countercases including flightless absent genera and a strong-flying Oedemerid; do not turn qualified pattern into universal law. Ignorance about mating fights and possible wear of tarsi explicit. P8 actual MathML is23/29 endemic genera, with without rechecking statistics qualifier; not integer2329. Raw are are typo retained. Punch cherub joke separate from entomological observation. Modern footnote dung-beetle characterization kept editorial, not substituted for Buprestidae discussion.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2133: Supplied November–December1857 tentative, not a precise date; all25 retained blocks, eight notes, annotations and bibliography read. Missing opening. Introductory imported/indigenous binary differs from finer single/double asterisk and ultra-indigenous classes in cited book. Does not independently know greater proportional variability in large genera, only obvious more species/more opportunities. Recommends Gyllenhal with species-reclassification caveat; Stephens dismissal opinion. Raw table independently inspected:20 rows,19 with four cells and final with two;39 catalogue-number/European-representative entries displayed in two side-by-side pairs. Do not merge adjacent entries into taxon pairs or interpret catalogue numbers as dates. Question marks, perhaps, ditto/abbreviations retained without expansions. Travel tomorrow, Bedford tillFriday thenIreland are plans. Footnote wider possible October1857–April1858 and reasons preferring late1857 retained rather than false certainty; Darwin list heading undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1640: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 2 with supplied 1855 year; complete twelve-page Wollaston letter, seventeen body blocks, read with all marginalia, footnotes and bibliography. A missing Darwin query arrived February 27; that is Wollaston receipt, not Darwin receipt of this reply. Ten answers cover possible Zargus/Calathus hybrid and damaged specimen, Dezerta geography/cultivation, Salvages sample uncertainty, widespread versus locally abundant insects, transitional families, variation, wings and Atlantis. Contrary to the Luna probe, P6 EXPLICITLY discusses five-jointed tarsi, Tomicidae and Anisotomidae; Waterhouse 1625 is a relevant comparison, but no Darwin use of that later memorandum is established. P8 permits adaptive wing change within fixed species limits, not endorsement of transmutation; P10 admits no measured same-island wing range. P11–13 explicitly state the four assumptions Darwin criticises in 1643. P14 distinguishes introduced winged and indigenous flightless species. Departure dates are alternatives, not realised travel. Later gift slip and hostile Origin review are separate apparatus.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
